info.bio:
Linkin Park es una banda estadounidense de rock procedente de Los Angeles, California, Estados Unidos. Formada en 1996, el grupo estuvo inicialmente integrado por Mike Shinoda, Dave Farrell, Joe Hahn, Brad Delson, Rob Bourdon y Mark Wakefield, este último como voz principal. La banda inició en ese mismo año sus primeros trabajos musicales de manera independiente y posterior a esto grabaron su primer material llamado Xero; sin embargo no tuvieron gran éxito en la búsqueda de un sello discográfico ya que ninguno mostró interés en su trabajo, lo que ocasionó la renuncia de Mark Wakefield. Poco después, Chester Bennington se incorporó a la banda como vocalista; el grupo realizó su primera presentación en un club de Los Ángeles y siendo respaldados por Jeff Blue, en aquel entonces vicepresidente de Warner Bros. Records, lograron firmar con el sello en 1999. El nombre del grupo es un juego de palabras haciendo referencia al Lincoln Park en Santa Mónica.

Los primeros años de la banda se remontan a un pequeño estudio del vocalista Mike Shinoda donde él, junto a un amigo y compañero de colegio Agoura High School, Brad Delson grabaron el primer material de la banda en 1995. Los dos estaban en el mismo instituto, donde conocieron a Rob Bourdon, actual baterista de la banda. Más adelante, cuando tomaron el tema de la banda más en serio, Shinoda contactó con Joe Hahn cuando estudiaba en el Art Center College de Pasadena. Por su parte, Delson compartió apartamento con el bajista David Farrell, quien decidió dejar el grupo, porque estaba comprometido con su otra formación. Farrell regresó un año más tarde. En esa época se unió a la banda Mark Wakefield, en 1996.

Ya en 1997 había seis integrantes en el grupo y decidieron llamarse SuperXero que posteriormente se veria resumida unicamente a Xero. Grabaron en la alcoba usada como estudio de Shinoda varias canciones con el fin de conseguir un contrato un sello discográfico. Aunque las compilaciones del Xero Sampler Tape se hicieron con pocos recursos, no pudo la banda conseguir un contrato y el proyecto no prosperó. La desilusión era tan grande dentro de la banda que por la misma razón Mark Wakefield decidió abandonar el grupo. Farrell, igual decidió abandonar el grupo por un tiempo, ya que su proyecto anteriormente dicho, la banda The Snax, tenía que hacer algunas giras, por lo que él les tenía que acompañar. Mientras eso se integra a la banda Kyle Christene, como bajista temporal.

Wakefield era vocalista de Xero, por lo que su salida provocó que el grupo consiguiera un nuevo cantante. Shinoda puso un anuncio en un periódico con el fin de contratar a un nuevo vocalista. Chester Bennington se interesó en aquel anuncio. Bennington es del estado de Arizona, estaba en el grupo Grey Daze y además empezó a grabar discos con el grupo mencionado anteriormente desde los 16 años. Recibió los demos del grupo, unos con las canciones interpretadas por otro vocalista y otro con las versiones instrumentales. Una vez terminado el trabajo de Bennington de grabar su voz en los demos instrumentales, los llamó avisando que estaba listo. Los de la banda le pidieron que una grabación que Bennington hizo la pusiera al teléfono. La banda quedó impresionada por su voz, por lo que decidieron convocarlo inmediatamente.

Tras la integración de Bennington en 1999, la banda se llamó Hybrid Theory. Desde entonces la banda se preocupó en hacer un nuevo material trabajando en un sello independiente. Pero al registrar el nombre del grupo, tuvieron un problema, ya que existía un grupo con el nombre Hybrid, por lo que la banda tuvo que cambiar su nombre otra vez. Después de tantos nombres, Bennington propuso que la banda se llamara Lincoln Park, donde pasaba con su auto al volver de los estudios, como un homenaje al Lincoln Park de Santa Monica. Desde entonces la banda se llamó Lincoln Park, pero hubo otro problema, ya que el dominio “lincolnpark.com” costaba más de lo que la banda podía permitir, cambiaron la palabra Lincoln por Linkin y desde ese momento se llamó la banda “Linkin Park” hasta el día de hoy.

Anteriormente estaban trabajando en un nuevo material lo que resultó ser un EP, llamado Hybrid Theory EP. Este EP contenía 6 canciones: Carousel, Technique, Step Up, And One, High Voltage y Part of Me. Fue lanzado el año 1999.

Linkin Park seguía por la lucha de la búsqueda de un contrato de sello discográfico, Hubo muchos rechazos por parte de grandes sellos discográficos. Jeef Blue los ayudó en esto. Éste en esa época se convirtió en el vicepresidente de Warner Bros. Records, desde entonces Linkin Park firmó un contrato con esta discográfica. Ya a la mano de Warner Bros., la banda trabajó para un nuevo material de estudio que se un año más tarde se lanzó. En la realización de este trabajo se integra Scott Koziol, bajista temporal de la banda. Éste trabajo sería uno de los mejores del grupo: Hybrid Theory.

Hybrid Theory (2000 - 2002)

El primer album de Linkin Park llamado Hybrid Theory fue lanzado el 24 de Octubre de 2000. Este disco le costó a Linkin Park medio año de trabajo. Su productor fue Don Gilmore. El disco tuvo un buen recibimiento por fanáticos. El grupo vendió más de 4,8 millones de copias sólo durante su año debut. El álbum está compuesto en mayoría por temas líricos que tratan los problemas que afectaron a Bennington durante su adolescencia, incluso el abuso de drogas y alcohol, el abuso infantil y el divorcio entre padres.

El disco fue #2 en el U.S. Billboard 200 y ha alcanzado posiciones muy buenas e importantes en el resto del mundo. La banda ha vendido alrededor de 24 millones de copias en todo el mundo, y de esos, 10 millones de copias se han vendido sólo en Estados Unidos, haciéndole el álbum de mejor venta en el siglo XXI.

En el 2001, Linkin Park formó parte en el Ozzfest, en el que estuvieron muchos artistas en gira, como Marilyn Manson, Slipknot, Crazy Town, Papa Roach, y Disturbed. Fue una época en que Linkin Park recibió muchas invitaciones para realizar giras de alto perfil como por ejemplo en el recién mencionado Ozzfest, en el Family Values Tour y en el KROQ Almost Acoustic Christmas. La banda inició su propia gira llamada Projekt Revolution, en la que participaron artistas invitados como Cypress Hill, Ademas, DJ Z-Trip, Xzibit, Mudvayne, Blindside y Snoop Dogg. Dentro de un año, Linkin Park había realizado más de 320 conciertos. También en el 2001, el bajista Koziol sale del grupo ya que vuelve Farrell.

Volviendo al tema de la discografía, Linkin Park lanzó una edición especial de su disco Hybrid Theory el 11 de Marzo de 2002 en Japón. Esta edición especial contiene todo el disco Hybrid Theory, además de 3 canciones (“Papercut”, “Points of Authority” y “A Place for My Head”) en vivo desde Docklands Arena, Londres, un nuevo tema “My December” y también un tema de del Hybrid Theory EP, solo que esta version fue remezclada, agregandole un background musical totalmente distinto y un bridge donde aparece Chester Bennington “High Voltage”.

Más adelante, en ese mismo año, el 30 de julio, Linkin Park lanzó un nuevo disco de remezclas titulado Reanimation. Este disco presenta remixes de canciones de Hybrid Theory e Hybrid Theory EP. Reanimation recibió la colaboración de numerosos artistas, como Black Thought, Jonathan Davis, Aaron Lewis, entre otros. A pesar de que este disco se hizo de material viejo del grupo, fue disco de platino en Estados Unidos vendiendo 1 millón de copias. Sólo en su semana debut vendió casi 270.000 copias.

Se hicieron muchos conciertos y giras en el mundo, hasta que en el propio autobús de la gira, la banda empezó a trabajar en un nuevo álbum: Meteora.

Meteora (2002 - 2004) 

Linkin Park siguió en giras y conciertos como se había dicho anteriormente, y debido a que seguirían así por mucho tiempo, la banda decidió trabajar en su nuevo álbum en el mismo autobús de la gira y usarlo como un estudio. La banda trabajó en el nuevo álbum entre su horario saturado y también en su tiempo libre.

La banda anunció la producción de un nuevo álbum de estudio en Diciembre de 2001 y revela su nuevo trabajo inspirado por la región rocosa de Meteora en Grecia donde se han construido numerosos monasterios encima de las piedras. Meteora ofrecía nuevamente el Rapcore y Nu metal, como en Hybrid Theory pero con la incorporación de nuevos y novedosos instrumentos, como un Shakuhashi (una flauta japonesa hecha de bambú) y nuevos efectos de sonido. Algo interesante es que la sincronización de las canciones del álbum se da en casi todo el disco.

El productor del álbum Meteora fue nuevamente Don Gilmore. La banda trabajó casi todo el año 2002 en el álbum, hasta diciembre del mismo año.

El segundo álbum de Linkin Park se lanzó mundialmente el 25 de Marzo de 2003. En el día de su debut ganó un reconocimiento mundial, ya que fue #1 en Estados Unidos y Reino Unido y #2 en Australia. La banda vendió más de 800.000 copias en la primera semana. En Octubre de 2003 se vendieron casi 3 millones de copias. Tuvo un éxito de ventas este álbum, claro que la banda recibió fuertes críticas. Según Allmusic.com dice que “No es nada más ni nada menos que Hybrid Theory Parte 2” y Blender lo califica como “más duro, más denso, más feo”.

El álbum permitió a Linkin Park a hacer una nueva gira Projekt Revolution, invitando artistas como Mudvayne, Blindside, y Xzibit. También en el 2003 Metallica lo invitó junto a Limp Bizkit, Mudvayne y Deftones a participar en el Summer Sanitarium Tour 2003. Linkin Park lanzó ese mismo año un álbum que contenía un CD y un DVD, estos tenían título Live In Texas que recopilaba las actuaciones que tuvo Linkin Park en Texas. En el año 2004 la banda hizo nuevamente una gira por todo el mundo llamada Meteora World Tour. El 29 de Junio de ese mismo año la banda lanza un nuevo disco, llamado Meteora Tour Edition, que contiene las canciones de Meteora en versiones en vivo que se dieron por todo el mundo en el Meteora World Tour.

Minutes to Midnight (2007)

Linkin Park intervino en el "Summer Sonic Festival" de Japón el 12 y el 13 de agosto de 2006. El 6 de marzo de 2007, Mike Shinoda publicó en su MySpace y en el de Linkin Park un post acerca del nuevo álbum llamado Minutes to Midnight, que se lanzó el 15 de mayo (2007) en Estados Unidos y el 14 de mayo en los demás países.

El primer sencillo What I've Done fue lanzado el 2 de abril de 2007. El álbum muestra Rock Alternativo mas "suave" (a comparacion de los albumes anteriores) con el que gran parte de su público se ha sentido decepcionado y algunos no tanto, alegando una evolución en su sonido. Su productor es Rick Rubin quien ha trabajado con Red Hot Chili Peppers, Audioslave, Metallica, Weezer, System of a Down,Limp Bizkit, Satanica, U2 y muchos otros. Hasta la fecha han salido cuatro sencillos más. El ultimo de estos Leave Out All The Rest una de las tantas baladas melódicas junto con Shadow Of The Day, incluidas en este disco. Minutes To Midnight ha ganado más de 20 Discos de Oro y algunos de Platino, superando el récord de Madonna. Actualmente se encuentran de gira con este nuevo trabajo, presumiblemente hasta comienzos de 2009.

A Thousand Suns (2010)

En el 2008, Chester anunció en una entrevista para MTV que el cuarto trabajo de estudio sería un «álbum conceptual». La banda volvió a los estudios de grabación en el año 2009, a partir de entonces y como prueba de ello comenzaron a publicar de manera frecuente información a modo de acertijo de una forma no muy clara en los cuales revelaba algo sobre el nuevo álbum de la banda. Shinoda dijo a la revista IGN que el nuevo álbum sería de un «género que revienta», también mencionó que sería más experimental y de vanguardia. El 7 de julio de 2009, Chester confirmó que Rick Rubin regresaría como productor en el nuevo álbum. En el Festival MTV Ululame, MTV entrevistó a Chester y comentó que el nuevo disco de Linkin Park posiblemente estaría en el mercado para junio de 2010.

A Thousand Suns fue confirmado el 8 de julio, se anunció que saldría el 14 de septiembre de 2010 en Estados Unidos en la página oficial de la banda, cuyo primer sencillo fue «The Catalyst», el cual se lanzó oficialmente al mercado el 2 de agosto del mismo año. En julio de 2010, la empresa desarrolladora de videojuegos Electronic Arts anunció que este sencillo formaría parte de la banda sonora del juego Medal of Honor.156 157 Al ya estar disponible en el mercado, A Thousand Suns encabezó los gráficos en varios países, incluyendo el Billboard 200, ya que vendió más de 241 000 copias en su primera semana. El álbum debutó en el número dos en Reino Unido habiendo vendido 46 711, copias siendo superado por el álbum Science & Faith de la banda The Script.

Para la promoción del disco, la banda inició una gira de conciertos que comenzó en Los Ángeles el 7 de septiembre. El 5 de octubre de 2010 fue publicado en iTunes el segundo sencillo, «Waiting for the End».165 Además, un documental llamado A Thousand Suns: the full experience acerca de la publicación del álbum, el cual estuvo disponible en el MySpace de la banda. En Francia, el álbum llegó a la cuarta posición, que es sin embargo inferior a los dos anteriores álbumes. El tercer sencillo del álbum, «Burning in the Skies», fue lanzado el 24 de febrero de 2011. El vídeo musical se estrenó en MTV el 21 de marzo de 2011 y fue dirigido por Joe Hahn.

El 13 de abril de 2011, Shinoda confirmó el cuarto sencillo del álbum, «Iridescent». También dijo que habría otra versión ligeramente más corta de la canción para la banda sonora de la película Transformers: el lado oscuro de la luna.168 El vídeo musical fue también dirigido por Joe Hahn y se estrenó el 3 de junio de 2011 en la página web de MTV y poco más tarde en YouTube. Linkin Park llegó al número ocho en el Billboard Social 50, una lista de los artistas más activos en las principales redes sociales del mundo. En los gráficos de fin de año, la banda llegó a número noventa y dos en la lista de artistas principales, así como también alcanzó el número cincuenta y tres en la lista Billboard 200 y el número siete en la lista de álbumes de rock, no obstante, «The Catalyst» obtuvo la posición número cuarenta en la lista de canciones de rock, todas pertenecientes a la revista Billboard.

En 2010, iniciaron su gira A Thousand Suns Tour, iniciando conciertos por primera vez en Sudamérica, donde visitaron Argentina y Chile el 7 y 9 de octubre respectivamente. También estuvieron el 11 de octubre en Brasil, donde ya habían tocado por única vez en 2004, durante la gira de Meteora. Igualmente realizaron actuaciones por Europa, Asia y Oceanía. En 2011 el grupo fue nominado en seis categorías en los premios Billboard, que fueron: top dúo/grupo, álbum de rock, artista rock, artista alternativo, canción alternativa por «Waiting for the End» y álbum alternativo, pero no ganó ningún premio.


Living Things y Recharged (2011-2013)

En junio de 2011, Chester reveló a la revista Kerrang! que Linkin Park había comenzado a trabajar en nuevo material para su próximo álbum. Explicó: «Hemos estado trabajando en un nuevo disco. La música es genial y estamos mucho más avanzados de lo que esperábamos estar. No hay muchos ruidos, pero hay muchas buenas canciones. Probablemente genere una reacción polarizada. Lo cual me complace. Como artista espero una reacción». El cantante agregó que lo que buscaban en el disco era hacer frente a temas controversiales, en lugar de [tratar] los asuntos personales que se tocaban en sus primeros álbumes de estudio. «Nosotros hemos aprendido a escribir canciones y letras serias, hemos aprendido a tratar con la política, fe y otras cosas».

Rick Rubin fue nuevamente el productor del material. Este dijo: «Una vez a la semana nos reuniremos a escuchar todo el material que tengamos y debatiremos sobre ello, esto para no cometer algunos errores que se cometieron en el proceso de grabación de los últimos dos álbumes».  En julio de 2011, Chester le dijo a la Rolling Stone que Linkin Park apuntaba para producir un nuevo álbum cada dieciocho meses, y que él se sorprendería si el nuevo álbum no estuviera listo para el 2012. La banda continuó grabando y produciendo el material incluso mientras se encontraban de gira, algo similar a lo acontecido en el proceso de grabación de su álbum Meteora. En marzo de 2012 el vocalista de la banda habló para la revista Kerrang! sobre el nuevo álbum diciendo: «Nos volvimos locos en nuestro anterior disco, A Thousand Suns, fue un disco experimental que por mucho tiempo polarizó a los seguidores de Linkin Park, pero el grupo es consciente de sus acciones». Esta producción no tuvo esos elementos musicales característicos de la banda, lo que condujo a una serie de desencantos para algunos. En el nuevo disco vamos a incorporar mucho trabajo con las guitarras, muchos coros y un sonido electrónico más pesado.

La banda reveló el día 28 de marzo en su página oficial, que el primer sencillo del álbum se llamaría «Burn It Down»; el cual fue lanzado el 16 de abril de 2012.  Mike Shinoda confirmó el 15 de abril en su blog oficial que el quinto disco se llamaría Living Things, el cual fue resultado de la mezcla de todos los sonidos y gustos de cada uno de los miembros de la agrupación, haciendo referencia a que es la vuelta al «auténtico Hybrid Theory», refiriéndose al gusto de la banda a la hora de mezclar sonidos. Este álbum se lanzó el 26 de junio del 2012.

El primer vídeoclip del álbum fue el del sencillo «Burn It Down». El segundo vídeo fue del segundo sencillo, «Lost in the Echo», que se estrenó el 29 de agosto de 2012, mientras que el tercero fue el de «Castle of Glass» en conjunto con el videojuego Medal of Honor: Warfighter, estrenado el 10 de octubre.

En mayo de 2013 Bennington confirmó su colaboración con la banda Stone Temple Pilots en una serie de presentaciones, además de grabar el EP High Rise fungiendo como nuevo integrante de la misma; sin embargo aseguró que Linkin Park «sigue siendo su prioridad»,185 186 dicho álbum fue lanzado el 8 de octubre 2013 bajo el nombre de «Stone Temple Pilots con Chester Bennington»,187 dicho álbum contiene los sencillos «Out of Time» y «Black Heart».188

El 29 de octubre de ese mismo año Linkin Park publicó su segundo álbum remix en el cual se incluyen versiones de su predecesor Living Things, este material fue lanzado en distintos formatos; disco compacto, disco de vinilo y descarga digital.


The Hunting Party (2014)

La banda está trabajando actualmente en la banda sonora de la pelicula ''Mall'', dirigida por Joe Hahn. En una entrevista con Fuse, Mike Shinoda indicó que se comenzó a trabajar en su sexto álbum.

Shinoda insinuo recientemente en una entrada de su blog que el sexto album sera lanzado en el 2014. En marzo de 2014, Linkin Park lanzó un nuevo sencillo titulado «Guilty All the Same», el tema cuenta con cuenta con la colaboración de Rakim, siendo el primer sencillo del sexto album. Mas tarde fue revelado que se llamaria ''THe Hunting Party'' y se lanzaría 17 de junio de 2014.


One More Light (2017)

Linkin Park comenzó a trabajar en material para un nuevo álbum en noviembre de 2015. En septiembre de 2016, el cantante Chester Bennington declaró: «Tenemos un montón de buen material que espero que desafíe a nuestra base de fanes, así como que los inspire tanto como nos inspira a nosotros».​ A principios de 2017, y durante una sesión de preguntas y respuestas, el cantante Mike Shinoda reveló que el álbum sonará distinto a trabajos anteriores de la banda: «Tienen que esperar lo inesperado».​ El guitarrista Brad Delson opinó sobre el álbum: «Hemos hecho tantos álbumes que sabemos con claridad cómo hacer uno, y definitivamente no tomamos el camino fácil con este».En febrero de 2017, la banda publicó vídeos promocionales en sus cuentas de redes sociales, en los que se los mostraba preparando nuevo material para el álbum.​ El primer sencillo del nuevo álbum, que se publicó el 16 de febrero de 2017, se llama «Heavy» y cuenta con la colaboración de la cantante de pop Kiiara.​ Como ya ha hecho en el pasado, la banda publicó mensajes enigmáticos sobre la publicación del nuevo disco; la portada del álbum fue revelada a través de puzles digitales en las redes sociales. La imagen que se desveló es la de seis chicos jugando en la playa.


Estilo de música

Tanto Hybrid Theory como Meteora tuvieron sonido Nu Metal y con influencias y elementos de Rock Industrial, Synth rock, Electronica, batería y bajo, utilizando progamadores y sintetizadores.

En el álbum Minutes to Midnight, la banda experimentó con sus sonidos establecidos más influencias de varios géneros de música y estilos. El periódico Los Angeles Times los compara con el trabajo de U2. En este mismo álbum solo en dos canciones se rapea. También es el primer álbum que presenta solos de guitarra y a Mike Shinoda cantando en lugar de rapear.

El uso de los dos tipos de canto de Linkin Park ha hecho gran parte de su música. Chester Bennington es muy conocido por sus gritos nu metal aunque también utiliza canto melódico y tiene el 46º lugar en la lista de cantantes de heavy metal "Heavy Metal's All-Time Top 100 Vocalists" de la revista Hit Parader. Mike Shinoda es el rapero de la banda. También hace coros en algunas canciones, pero en el nuevo álbum ha cantado en tres canciones; ha estado en la lista de "Heavy Metal's All-Time Top 100 Vocalists" en 72º lugar.

En su último trabajo, Living Things, se puede notar un cambio a un Rock Experimental. En este disco todos participan en los coros y es la primera vez en la que se escucha a Brad Delson cantando en una de sus canciones (Until it Breaks).

podcast.title: Malaysia Seated Show – October 15, 2003, Kuala Lumpur, 50,000 Fans, No Screaming, No Movement
podcast.body: When Linkin Park was booked to play Merdeka Stadium in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, on October 15, 2003, significant religious opposition arose from groups arguing that rock music corrupted youth. Negotiations with the government produced an "artist performance ethics document" requiring: audiences to remain seated at all times with no dancing or jumping; stage decoration limited to a simple backdrop with the band's logo; the band dressed from chest to knees with no exposed skin and no clothing linked to drugs; no swearing, violent, or erotic behavior; no "leaping around or throwing something from the stage"; the band seated during the entire performance; and no screaming during any songs. Linkin Park accepted all conditions. The show proceeded before 50,000 similarly seated fans, with police present both inside and for the religious demonstrators outside. "Can you imagine a Linkin Park show without screaming and jumping and dancing and swearing?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Contemporaries in 2004
podcast.body: Linkin Park was among the artists who had records out in the spring of 2004, during a period when Modest Mouse's unconventional song offered a contrasting sound. "If you weren't in music in the spring of 2004, you might remember how this song stood out amongst records by Green Day and You too and Lincoln Park."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Extended Hiatus (2004-2007)
podcast.body: Following intense touring and recording through 2004, Linkin Park took an almost four-year break from releasing proper studio albums. During this hiatus, individual band members pursued various side projects and collaborations to maintain their creative output. "by the end of 2004 Lincoln Park needed a break. So they disappeared for almost four solid years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: 2005 Warner Music Group Dispute
podcast.body: In spring 2005, Warner, the band's record label, requested they perform at the New York Stock Exchange to celebrate its IPO following a significant financial restructuring that included $250 million in cuts. Lincoln Park was incensed by the cuts, believing they would hinder the label's ability to promote their music and other artists, and publicly refused to play, highlighting that they received no share from the IPO despite having sold 57 million records with just two albums. "Lincoln Park, though, was pissed at this one."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Favorable Contract Renegotiation (2005)
podcast.body: After a public dispute with Warner Music Group, Lincoln Park secured a $15 million advance for their next album, "Minutes to Midnight," and an option for up to five additional albums with an exceptionally high royalty rate of 20%. Warner had little choice but to agree, given their new presence in financial markets and the risk of losing "the biggest rock band in the world at the time." "Lincoln Park had a $15 million advance for the next album which was Minutes to Midnight. They were also given an option for up to 5 more albums with a royalty rate of 20%, which is a pretty insanely high rate."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Record Label Dispute with Warner Brothers (2005)
podcast.body: Between 2003 and 2007, Linkin Park was embroiled in a public and contentious dispute with Warner Brothers Records, which significantly delayed their third album. The band alleged that only a small portion of the money from Warner's stock offering would benefit artists, while the label accused the band of "extortion" for demanding a $60 million advance. Linkin Park sued Warner to exit their seven-album contract, but the lawsuit was dropped in December 2005 after negotiations, with both sides agreeing to keep the specifics confidential. "A rift had opened between the band and their management and Warner Brothers records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Cell Phone Account Control Seized (August 2006)
podcast.body: In August 2006, Chester received an email from his cell phone provider confirming a successful password change on his account, which he had not authorized. Despite Chester's preference for paper bills and having no previous online account management, the stalker had created an online account for him, changed its password, and then changed it again after Chester tried to revert it. "Then in August 2006, Chester got an email from his cell phone provider, confirming that he had successfully changed his password on his account."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Uncharted "Sneak Peak" - Episode 7: The Linkin Park Cyberstalker

podcast.title: Chester Bennington's Cell Phone Hacked (Late March 2006)
podcast.body: The band's cyberstalking crisis began in late March 2006 when Linkin Park vocalist Chester Bennington had his cell phone hacked. This incident occurred during an earlier technological era, predating the widespread use of iPhones and modern cybersecurity features like two-factor authentication, facial recognition, and strong password reminders. "In late March of that year, Lincoln Park vocalist Chester Bennington had his cell phone hacked."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Uncharted "Sneak Peak" - Episode 7: The Linkin Park Cyberstalker

podcast.title: Cybersecurity Nightmare and National Security Crisis (Spring 2006)
podcast.body: The hacking of Chester Bennington's phone and subsequent events plunged him and his wife, Talinda, into a cybersecurity nightmare. This situation transcended personal privacy issues, ultimately impacting America's national security apparatus and involving facilities related to its nuclear arsenal. "It was a situation that affected America's national security apparatus, and, like I said, involved its nuclear arsenal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Uncharted "Sneak Peak" - Episode 7: The Linkin Park Cyberstalker

podcast.title: Email Harassment to Talinda (Spring 2006)
podcast.body: As Chester was away with the band, Talinda received another direct email containing highly personal and disturbing content, stating, "I know you're going through a hard time being alone, My thoughts and prayers are with you." This message strongly intimated that the sender had unauthorized access to Chester's touring schedule and the couple's personal life, with such emails continuing throughout Spring 2006, confirming persistent compromises of their privacy. "This was followed by another email sent directly to Talinda when Chester was out of town with the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Uncharted "Sneak Peak" - Episode 7: The Linkin Park Cyberstalker

podcast.title: Identity Theft by Nuclear Lab Technologist – Devon Townsend, Albuquerque, 2006
podcast.body: In late winter 2006, Chester Bennington's wife Talinda began receiving threatening calls and texts, friends were called from the hacked number, and Talinda lost access to her eBay and PayPal accounts. Chester hired a former Secret Service specialist who traced the intrusion to a 27-year-old single mother named Devon Townsend, employed as a technologist at a nuclear weapons research facility in New Mexico. Townsend had initially found Chester's email address in a mass email accidentally sent out to promote a tattoo parlor Chester co-owned in Tempe, Arizona. She used his birthday and zip code to access his .Mac account, then guessed his password as "Charlie" (his middle name), gaining access to email addresses, photos, home addresses, social security numbers, and bank account details — though she did not steal any money. She was arrested and charged with multiple offenses. "She was a fan. And she was bored at her job."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Impersonation via Email (Spring 2006)
podcast.body: Talinda's friends started receiving unusual emails supposedly from her, which contained details and writing styles inconsistent with Talinda's own. Talinda confirmed she had not sent these messages, tracing their origin to a Yahoo account she had ceased using months prior, indicating it had been compromised. "Apparently they were receiving strange messages from her, detailing things that Talinda would not write."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Uncharted "Sneak Peak" - Episode 7: The Linkin Park Cyberstalker

podcast.title: Informant Email to a Friend (April 6, 2006)
podcast.body: Approximately two weeks after the initial email to Talinda, on April 6, 2006, a male friend of the couple (who had previously dated Talinda) received a more ominous email from "Informant for you at Yahoo.com." This email contained private facts that should have been known only to Chester, Talinda, and their closest associates, signaling a serious breach of privacy. "A couple heard from a male friend, someone who had dated Talinda in the past, that he'd had a similar sort of email, one from the address, Informant for you at Yahoo.com."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Uncharted "Sneak Peak" - Episode 7: The Linkin Park Cyberstalker

podcast.title: Initial Suspicious Email to Talinda (Spring 2006)
podcast.body: The events that started the crisis for Talinda began when she received an email from an unrecognized address. The email contained a message like "I'm very happy for you and Chester" and included a link to a website belonging to Chester's ex-wife, Samantha. Talinda initially dismissed this as the work of a typical online troll, a common occurrence for rock stars and their partners. "It all began when Talinda opened an email from an address she didn't recognize."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Uncharted "Sneak Peak" - Episode 7: The Linkin Park Cyberstalker

podcast.title: Leak of Child Custody Information (Spring/Summer 2006)
podcast.body: Emails from the "informant Yahoo account" persistently contained highly sensitive and private information about the Bennington's personal lives. This included extremely private details, specifically mentioning a child custody issue they were experiencing, demonstrating the depth of the stalker's unauthorized access. "Each contained information about the Bennington's that should have been very private, right down to a child custody issue that they were having."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Uncharted "Sneak Peak" - Episode 7: The Linkin Park Cyberstalker

podcast.title: Midnight Phone Calls (Spring 2006)
podcast.body: Chester began receiving late-night phone calls on his mobile, typically between 4:00 AM and 4:30 AM, but no one would speak when he answered. Upon checking the caller ID and calling the number back, he reached a switchboard operator in New Mexico who could not trace the origin of the call, leading to Chester's frustration. "Chester's mobile would bring in the middle of the night, usually between 4 and 4 30 AM, but when he answered it, no one was there."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Uncharted "Sneak Peak" - Episode 7: The Linkin Park Cyberstalker

podcast.title: PayPal Account Targeted (Summer 2006)
podcast.body: Following the eBay incident, Chester and Talinda received a notification from PayPal. This alert confirmed that someone had attempted to change the password on their PayPal account, indicating multiple financial platforms were being targeted. "They got a notification from PayPal that someone had tried to change the password on that account."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Uncharted "Sneak Peak" - Episode 7: The Linkin Park Cyberstalker

podcast.title: Stalker Impersonates Talinda to Security (Spring 2006)
podcast.body: Bruce Thompson, Linkin Park's head of security at the time, received an email purporting to be from Talinda, inquiring about Chester's ex-wife Samantha's email address and mentioning "Strange emails from fansources have been received" with "a lot of information." Bruce initially believed Talinda sent the message, but it was later revealed to be from the mystery cyberstalker. "Back then, Lincoln Park had a head of security, his name was Bruce Thompson, and he got an email that was supposed to be from Talinda."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Stalker's Message in Password Field (August 2006)
podcast.body: After gaining access to Chester's cell phone account, the victims discovered a chilling message deliberately left by the perpetrator. In the field where the password should have been, the stalker had typed: "Who is doing this to you?" "When they logged on, they found something written in the field where the password should have been."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Threatening Call to Talinda (Spring 2006)
podcast.body: A few nights after the silent calls began, Talinda answered Chester's cell phone to hear a female voice deliver a chilling message: "I'm watching you, horror." This call also featured a blocked caller ID, indicating an intentional effort to conceal the stalker's identity. "A few nights after that Chester's cell phone rang again, and this time Talinda answered, a female voice said, I'm watching you, horror."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: eBay Account Hacked (Summer 2006)
podcast.body: At a later point, Talinda attempted to access the couple's eBay account but was denied entry, discovering that someone had changed the password. This incident further demonstrated the comprehensive nature of the cyberstalking and identity theft attempts. "A little later, Talinda tried to log on to the couple's eBay account, but you couldn't get in because someone had changed the password."

Footage from the event showed Chester Bennington appearing happy and healthy just days before his death. "On July 14, 2017, the band shot an episode of Carpool Karaoke with James Corden. podcast.title: Chester Bennington Tribute Concert (2017)
podcast.body: On October 27, 2017, a three-hour tribute concert for Chester Bennington was held at the Hollywood Bowl. The event featured friends from Blink 182, System of a Down, Korn, and Avenged Sevenfold, and was streamed live, reaching millions of viewers as Linkin Park paid tribute to their fallen bandmate. "On October 27th, 2017, there was a three hour tribute to Chester featuring his friends from Blink 182, system of a downed corn, a bench, seven fold and more."

podcast.title: Chester Bennington's Suicide (2017)
podcast.body: Chester Bennington committed suicide on July 20, 2017, after returning to Linkin Park from his temporary role in Stone Temple Pilots. "But then we all know what happened next, Chester committed suicide on July 20th of 2017."

podcast.title: Return with Lineup Changes (2024)
podcast.body: After a long hiatus following Chester Bennington's death, Linkin Park reportedly returned to the music scene in late 2024, featuring a couple of lineup changes. This marked the band's official re-emergence after a period of adjusting to the loss of their former frontman. "It was only in late 2024 that they returned with a couple of lineup changes."

podcast.title: 21st Century Rock Success
podcast.body: Linkin Park was included as a potential example of a band from the first decade of the 21st century that could be considered among the "alt rock giants" of earlier decades, in a broader discussion about the music industry's struggle to create new superstars. "Now think about it, outside of Coldplay, Jack White, Gorillas and maybe Lincoln Park. Who else from the first decade of the 21st century can rank against the alt rock giants of the 80s and 90s?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: 21st Century Success from New Metal
podcast.body: Linkin Park emerged indirectly from the late 1990s nu-metal scene and went on to become one of the biggest bands of the 21st century, demonstrating the lasting impact of rock-hip hop cross-pollination. "the whole new metal thing at the end of the 1990s which indirectly gave birth to Lincoln Park, still one of the biggest bands of the 21st century."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 3: The New Genres

podcast.title: 8-bit Rebellion iOS Game
podcast.body: In April 2009, Linkin Park launched an iOS application called "8-bit Rebellion," which was a video game featuring the band members as characters. The game included an exclusive song, "Blackbirds," obtainable only by successfully completing the game. "In April 2009, they released an iOS app called 8-bit Rebellion, which was a video game featuring band members as characters."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Advanced Online Presence (Early 2010s)
podcast.body: In the early 2010s, Linkin Park benefited from a highly capable management team that was notably advanced in its approach to social media and online fan engagement compared to most contemporary acts. This team was also very proactive and aware of the critical need for robust security measures. "They were smart, way ahead of what most acts were doing at the time with things like social media and online fan engagement."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Uncharted "Sneak Peak" - Episode 7: The Linkin Park Cyberstalker

podcast.title: Album Release Delays
podcast.body: The release of their third album, Minutes to Midnight, was originally slated for mid-2006 but was delayed until May 14, 2007. The band's substantial success afforded them the ability to delay the release without adverse consequences. "The original release date was in mid 2006, but because they were such a very successful band, they could get away with delaying it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Backmasking in Digital Era
podcast.body: Linkin Park is an artist mentioned as using backward messages, a trend that revived with the widespread availability of digital sound editing software from the late 1990s onwards. "Back, cake, cold play, M&M, Fransford Nand, Lincoln Park, Marilyn Manson, Moby Soundgarden Tool, 21 Pilots, and a ton more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Band Origin in Agoura Hills
podcast.body: The core of Linkin Park began with three high school friends—Mike Shinoda, Brad Delson, and Rob Bourdon—who attended Agoura Hills High School, located approximately 30 miles northwest of downtown Los Angeles. "Everything with his band starts at a high school in Agora Hills, which is about 30 miles northwest of downtown Los Angeles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Band's Stand Against Label Interference
podcast.body: In an unusual move for a new band, Linkin Park directly met with Warner Brothers executives and firmly rejected various label suggestions, including demands to remove rapping, change Mike Shinoda's rap style to mimic Fred Durst, bring in a reggae vocalist named Matt Lyons, or introduce gimmicks for DJ Joe Hahn like wearing a cowboy hat and lab coat. They also refused to change their logo, which some at the label found "too Asian." "And the meeting was risky because new bands just don't show up in the boardrooms of major record labels and start dictating terms for how they were to be marketed and how their fan club should be treated."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Best-Selling American Rock Band of the 21st Century
podcast.body: As of 2008, Linkin Park was recognized as the best-selling American rock band of the 21st century, having sold 35-38 million records worldwide since their debut album in 2000. Nickelback was noted as the only other band to approach these sales figures in a comparable timeframe. "This is the story of the best-selling American Rock Band of the 21st Century."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Biggest Selling Modern Rock Act (2000s)
podcast.body: By spring 2005, the band was "on their way to becoming the biggest selling modern rock act of the decade." "Lincoln Park was on their way to becoming the biggest selling modern rock act of the decade."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 14

podcast.title: Career Record Sales
podcast.body: Linkin Park is described as an old-school style superstar rock band that has sold over 100 million records in their career. "Lincoln Park, an old school style superstar rock band who have sold, wait for it, more than a hundred million records in their career."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Trying to be a Superstar in the 21st Century

podcast.title: Charity Work
podcast.body: Linkin Park actively engaged in various charity efforts, including supporting victims of the Asian tsunami and Hurricane Katrina, and participating in the Live 8 event. "Not to mention some charity work with everything from Asian tsunami and hurricane Katrina victims to participating in the Live 8 event."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Chester Bennington's Return
podcast.body: Chester Bennington left Stone Temple Pilots on November 9, 2015, to return to Linkin Park. The plan was for him to rejoin STP after Linkin Park's next project was complete. "Chester left the group amicably on November 9th, 2015 to go back to Lincoln Park."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Groups That Changed Their Front-Person and Survived

podcast.title: Chester Bennington's Role in STP
podcast.body: Chester Bennington of Linkin Park began filling in as the vocalist for Stone Temple Pilots after Scott Weiland's official termination from the band. "Wyland's gun solo, and Chester Bennington of Lincoln Park started filling in."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Continued Activity in 2010s
podcast.body: This established band continued its characteristic musical output throughout the 2010s, contrasting with the softer pop alt-rock trend. "Older groups, the food fighters, Lincoln Park, Black Keys, Chili Peppers, Green Day, Queens of the Stone Age, Royal Blood, Muse, Blink 182, Pearl Jam, they just kept doing what they did best."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

podcast.title: Creative Break and Side Projects
podcast.body: After the intense touring cycle for Meteora, the band collectively requested and took downtime. This period allowed members to rest and "pursue some other projects" (like Chester Bennington's Dead by Sunrise and the Jay-Z collaboration "Collision Course") to revitalize their creative energies. "Besides, it would be good to rest and then maybe pursue some other projects to restore the creative juices."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Decreased Rap in Minutes to Midnight
podcast.body: For their *Minutes to Midnight* album, the band intentionally reduced the amount of rap, with Mike Shinoda rapping on only two of the 12 songs. This decision was made because the "new metal" genre was perceived as "dead," and the band was uncertain about fan acceptance of rap in the evolving music landscape. "The new metal was dead so the amount of wrapping that fans might find acceptable was uncertain. So taking the safe route, they toned it down."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Career Success & Control
podcast.body: By 2011, approximately 10 years after forming, Lincoln Park had sold over 80 million albums and amassed millions of fans globally. They exercised firm control over their career, dictating a schedule of releasing a new album every 18 months, rather than their record label. "In the 10 years since the band was formed, they'd sold over 80 million albums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Success Amidst Piracy
podcast.body: Despite the "all-time peak" of illegal file sharing platforms like Napster, LimeWire, and Kazaa when their first two albums were released, Linkin Park achieved immense commercial success, selling a combined 57 million copies worldwide from Hybrid Theory and Meteora. "But for God's sake, 57 million in sales from just two albums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Embraced Modern Electronic Drums
podcast.body: Rob Borden of Lincoln Park is one of the contemporary drummers who has adopted modern electronic drums. These instruments are utilized to trigger sounds, tones, patterns, and samples, demonstrating their versatility in modern music production and performance. "Today's electronic drums have been embraced by players such as Danny Carey, Neil Peart, Will Champion of Coldplay, Rob Borden of Lincoln Park, and many, many others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of the Modern Drum Kit

podcast.title: Emergence from New Metal
podcast.body: Linkin Park was one of the few groups to emerge from the late 1990s' "new metal" scene bigger and stronger, distinguishing themselves with a pop sensibility that made their angry and powerful music highly catchy. "Lincoln Park is pretty much the only group to emerge from the whole new metal thing of the late 90s bigger and stronger."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Emerging Big Band (2000s)
podcast.body: Linkin Park (transcribed as "Link-One-A-D2") is included in a list of bands that were "soon-to-be-big" around 2000-2001, playing a role in the broader rock music revival.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Emerging New Metal Offshoot
podcast.body: Linkin Park was introduced as a "new band out of LA" that, while not purely new metal, exhibited some of the genre's sonic trappings, suggesting their emergence as part of the broader new metal wave. "Crazy town, popper roach, disturbed, and this new band out of LA called Lincoln Park."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 00's Part 1: The Sad State of Rock

podcast.title: Extended Hiatus After Chester Bennington's Death
podcast.body: Following the death of lead singer Chester Bennington in July 2017, Linkin Park entered a prolonged period of inactivity as the remaining members grappled with the loss and adjusted to the tragedy. The band was absent from the music scene for a considerable time, with their eventual return in late 2024 accompanied by lineup changes. "Lincoln Park was absent from the scene for a long, long time after Chester's death as everybody tried to adjust."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 9: (20-11)

podcast.title: Extensive Documentation
podcast.body: Linkin Park's journey and story are exceptionally well-documented by various entities, including the band members themselves, their management company, their record label, and their dedicated fanbase. "Lincoln Park is a very 21st century band and the sense that their story is so very well documented by themselves, their management company, their label, and their fans."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Genre Evolution with Minutes to Midnight
podcast.body: With "Minutes to Midnight," Linkin Park made a deliberate choice to shift their sound away from "pure new metal" into "a different sort of headspace." This change was partly evidenced by Mike Shinoda's increased singing roles and reduced rapping, appearing on only two of the album's 12 songs. "Lincoln Park made a conscious decision to move away from pure new metal into a different sort of headspace."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: High Productivity Early Career
podcast.body: During the first couple of years of their career, Linkin Park maintained an "insane level of productivity," constantly touring while simultaneously writing and recording. For their second album, Meteora, they managed to demo at least 80 different songs over eight months, dodging in and out of the studio between shows. "That's an insane level of productivity."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Initial Label Disdain for Sound
podcast.body: Warner Brothers Records executives, including reportedly the label president, initially struggled to understand and even disliked Linkin Park's sound, characterized by "screaming and rapping." There was even internal debate about whether to release their debut record at all. "Warner did not know what to do with Lincoln Park and some, including apparently the president of the label just hated their sound."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Initial Record Label Rejections
podcast.body: Linkin Park was turned down by various record labels approximately four dozen times before being signed to Warner Brothers on their fourth attempt. Despite this persistence, most at the label, excluding the executive who championed them, did not expect the band to achieve significant success. "After being turned down about four dozen times by various record labels, and that is not an exaggeration, four dozen is the number. They were finally signed to Warner Brothers on their fourth try."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Initial Record Label Rejections
podcast.body: Their demos were turned down by record labels almost 50 times before they were signed at the end of 1999, which reflected the music industry's belief that new metal was "over" at that time. "And to think that their demos were turned down by record labels almost 50 times before they were signed at the end of 1999, that's how much the industry believed that new metal was over."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Inspired by Skinny Puppy
podcast.body: Linkin Park is explicitly listed as an artist who was inspired and influenced by the Canadian industrial band Skinny Puppy. "Here's a short list of artists who say they were inspired and influenced by Skinny Puppy, Ministry, Nine-inch Nails, Maryland Manson, the Prodigy, Ramstein, Filter, Corn, Lincoln Park, Evan Essence."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Intense Touring Schedule
podcast.body: In the year immediately following the release of their debut album, Hybrid Theory, Linkin Park demonstrated an extraordinary work ethic by performing 320 shows. "In the first year after hybrid theory came out, they played 320 shows."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Intense Workload and Toll
podcast.body: The band's initial four years were characterized by an "insane" pace of continuous touring, writing, and recording, which inevitably took a significant toll on their mental well-being, physical health, and personal lives. "You can't keep up this kind of pace with other being some kind of toll on your mind, your health and your personal life."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Japanese Special Edition of Hybrid Theory
podcast.body: A unique two-disc version of Linkin Park's debut album, Hybrid Theory, was sold in Japan. The first disc contained the standard album, while the second disc featured a collection of unreleased live tracks and additional studio recordings. "there was a special two-disc version of hybrid theory sold in Japan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: LP Recharge Online Game
podcast.body: Chester Bennington was involved in the creation of "LP Recharge," an online action game based on the band itself. The game was launched through Facebook, demonstrating the band's engagement with new digital platforms. "He was also involved in the creation of LP Recharge, which was an online action game based on the band and launched through Facebook."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Live Album Production Challenges
podcast.body: The live album and DVD released for Christmas 2003 featured audio recorded solely in Houston on August 2, 2003, but incorporated video footage from both the Houston show and another performance in Dallas the following night. This mixing of visual sources with a single audio track resulted in "subtle changes in appearances by the band members" and other continuity issues. "All the video we see was shot in Houston and the next night in Dallas. The audio though is just from Houston."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Live Music Mention
podcast.body: Linkin Park was mentioned in the context of playing live music. No specific details about recordings, albums, or concerts were provided beyond the name. "How about this from Lincoln Park?"

podcast.title: Members' Side Projects
podcast.body: The band members, all in their 30s by 2011, found time to pursue various side projects, encompassing both musical and non-musical endeavors. These included remix albums, contributions to soundtracks, and even movies, with DJ Johan notably starting to direct films. "Plus, they had time to indulge in all kinds of side projects, some musical, some not, like remix album, soundtracks, even movies, DJ Johan had started to direct films."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Most Pirated Rock Artist
podcast.body: Linkin Park was identified as the most pirated rock act of the 2000s, with their music, particularly from the *Hybrid Theory* album, being widely shared illegally. "No one had their music pirated more apparently than Lincoln Park."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Most Successful New Metal Descendant
podcast.body: Linkin Park is considered the most successful of all the bands to descend from the new metal era, having created a superior and more cohesive hybrid of alternative rock and rap. "No other band ever created a better and more cohesive hybrid of alternative rock and rap than these guys."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Name Change from Hybrid Theory
podcast.body: The band changed their name to Linkin Park after Chester Bennington successfully auditioned and joined the group, subsequently launching their career. "He got that gig, the band changed their name to Lincoln Park, and everybody was off to the races."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Name Change from Hybrid Theory
podcast.body: The band changed its name to "Linkin Park" from "Hybrid Theory" after being inspired by an actual park of the same name in Santa Monica that they drove by daily. They believed it to be a universally recognizable name, as many American towns reportedly have a Lincoln Park. "Hybrid Theory became the deliberately misspelled Lincoln Park."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: New Metal Era Foundation
podcast.body: Linkin Park's existence and massive success (over 100 million records sold) would not have been possible had they not been "bored in the new metal era of the late 90s." "Lincoln Park would not have existed or sold 100 million records had they not been bored in the new metal era of the late 90s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: One More Light Fund Establishment
podcast.body: In memory of Chester Bennington, Linkin Park established the "One More Light Fund," an organization dedicated to offering help and support to individuals grappling with mental health issues. "And in Chester's memory, Lincoln Park has the one more light fund, an organization that offers help to those who need it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Online Savvy from Piracy
podcast.body: The challenge of widespread piracy compelled Linkin Park to develop one of the most sophisticated online presences among bands. This experience made them highly adept at managing piracy issues and engaging with their fanbase digitally. "piracy forced Lincoln Park to become one of the most savvy bands in the world when it came to online presence."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 10: (10-1)

podcast.title: Online Security History
podcast.body: While Linkin Park's management later became very conscious of security, the band's online presence was not always as secure as it is in the present day. This historical lack of comprehensive security contributed to significant vulnerabilities. "But the online world of Lincoln Park wasn't always as secure as it is today."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Uncharted "Sneak Peak" - Episode 7: The Linkin Park Cyberstalker

podcast.title: Pioneering Online Fan Club
podcast.body: Linkin Park established a high-level fan club and street team called "Linkin Park Underground," which focused on serving fans online. This dedication to online fan engagement was a novel approach for bands at the time. "They created a high-level fan club slash street team called Lincoln Park Underground that strove to serve the fans online, something that few bands were doing at the time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-1990s Release
podcast.body: Although born in the new metal era of the late 90s, the specific song mentioned came out in 2000, not the 90s. "Now to be very fair, that song came out in 2000 and not in the 90s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Project Revolution CD Initiative
podcast.body: During the Project Revolution tour in 2007-2008, Linkin Park implemented an innovative merchandise strategy: they sold blank CDs at their merch booths for $11, each containing a download code that allowed fans to download and burn that specific Linkin Park show for personal use. "Each came with a download code that allowed any fan to download and burn that particular Lincoln Park show for their personal use."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Project Revolution Tour
podcast.body: Linkin Park took the initiative to create and headline their own tour, "Project Revolution," which notably featured popular artists such as Snoop Dogg and Cypress Hill. "They created their own tour called Project Revolution, which featured Snoop Dogg and Saipers Hill."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Public Contract Negotiation
podcast.body: The band issued a press release criticizing Warner Music Group for an expected $1.4 billion windfall from their IPO, with only $7 million going to company operations and nothing to artists, while Warner fired back accusing the band's management of using "fictitious numbers" and "inflammatory threats" as a negotiating tactic. This public dispute lasted for months, drawing significant media attention. "This very public fight went on for months before an agreement was reached."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Radio Friendly Sound
podcast.body: Linkin Park was recognized for its broad appeal and "super radio friendly" sound, which distinguished them within the New Metal genre, even as the genre itself was largely declining. "Lincoln Park was super radio friendly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Record Deal with Warner Brothers
podcast.body: Linkin Park signed with Warner Brothers Records in late 1999, a deal facilitated by an A&R executive named Jeff who had previously recommended Chester Bennington to the band (then Zero) and later became a VP at Warner Brothers. This signing occurred despite Warner Brothers having rejected the band three times previously. "they got a meeting, and they were signed in late 1999."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Record Industry Evolution & Sales Decline
podcast.body: Over their career, the band witnessed a drastic shift in the record industry; their first album sold 30 million copies, but by their sixth album in 2014, worldwide sales barely reached a million. This decline in physical sales was attributed to streaming taking over, yet the band sustained itself through touring and a deep catalog. "By the time the numbers started coming in for their sixth album in 2014, World Wide Sales barely added up to a million."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Ringtone Popularity - Mid-2000s
podcast.body: In the mid-2000s, songs by artists like Linkin Park were constantly heard as ringtones in public spaces such as the subway, schools, hospitals, and streets. This reflected a widespread desire among young people to publicly display their musical tastes and individuality. Users would pay around 1.5 to 2 euros for a polyphonic ringtone by Linkin Park, considering it an investment in their personal brand. "Canciones de Metallica, Eminem, Fifth Dissent, Blint Note, Linkin Park, The Vanessens, sonaban constantemente en el metro, en el colegio, en el hospital, en la calle."

podcast.title: Sales Figures
podcast.body: Linkin Park has sold approximately 100 million records throughout their career, highlighting their significant commercial success. "This guy was the frontman for a band that sold somewhere around 100 million records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sophisticated Online & Social Media Strategy
podcast.body: Lincoln Park developed an exceptionally smart and effective online and social media organization, recognized for its modern 21st-century approach to engaging and maintaining their fanbase. The band members were deeply involved, constantly interacting, providing special content, and releasing music directly to fans. "I have never seen an organization smarter than the one behind Lincoln Park."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Strategic Name Change for Domain
podcast.body: In 1999, Linkin Park deliberately misspelled "Lincoln" in their name as "Linkin" to secure the readily available domain name, Lincolnpark.com. This approach to online branding was a forward-thinking strategy for a band at that time. "The reason they deliberately misspelled Lincoln, so they could get the domain, Lincolnpark.com."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Twilight Soundtracks Contribution
podcast.body: Linkin Park contributed to the various *Twilight* soundtracks that accompanied the film series. These soundtracks featured a nice selection of tunes, mostly album cuts and outtakes, from a range of artists spanning different genres. "The Paramore, Lincoln Park, Collective Soul, Death Cab for Cutie, Tom York, the Killers, Editors, Metric, Block Keys, Dead Weather, Beck, Vampire Weekend, Florence in the Machine."

xref.body: Chester toured and recorded with Stone Temple Pilots for two and a half years before amicably departing in November 2015. xref.body: In June and July 2017, Chester toured Europe with Linkin Park. Observers noted that he appeared to be in the best physical condition of his life during this period. "In June and July 2017, Lincoln Park toured Europe. The band was on fire. People remarked that Chester seemed to be in the best physical condition of his life."

xref.title: Chester Bennington Tribute Concert (2017)
xref.body: On October 27, 2017, a three-hour tribute concert for Chester Bennington was held at the Hollywood Bowl. The event featured friends from Blink 182, System of a Down, Korn, and Avenged Sevenfold, and was streamed live, reaching millions of viewers as Linkin Park paid tribute to their fallen bandmate. "On October 27th, 2017, there was a three hour tribute to Chester featuring his friends from Blink 182, system of a downed corn, a bench, seven fold and more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Death by Suicide (2017)
xref.body: Chester Bennington died on July 20, 2017, by hanging himself from a door in his bedroom, discovered by a housekeeper. The date of his death eerily coincided with what would have been Chris Cornell's 53rd birthday, suggesting a potential connection to Cornell's passing two months prior, which was described as breaking "something in Chester." Despite a vacation with his family in Arizona, Bennington returned to LA for an alleged Linkin Park video shoot, but "something went very wrong" that evening. No drugs or significant alcohol were found, and his autopsy revealed nothing of concern in his blood, leaving his motivations largely unknown. "The only possible clue is that July 20 would have been Chris Cornell's 53rd birthday."

xref.title: Date of Death and Cause
xref.body: Chester Bennington, the vocalist for Linkin Park, was confirmed dead by his own hand on Thursday, July 20, 2017. His death came as a shock and was widely considered unexpected, even among a series of other musician deaths around that time. "Chester Bennington, vocalist with Lincoln Park, was not only dead, but dead by his own hand."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Death Date Coincidence – 37 Years After Ian Curtis, Close to Chester Bennington
xref.body: Cornell died by hanging on May 18, 2017 — exactly 37 years to the day that Joy Division singer Ian Curtis hanged himself. Two months later, on July 20, 2017 (which would have been Cornell's 53rd birthday), his close friend Chester Bennington of Linkin Park died by suicide, also by hanging. Cornell is interred at Hollywood Forever Cemetery in Los Angeles; his tombstone reads "Voice of our generation and an artist for all time." Johnny Ramone's monument is nearby. "Two months after Chris died, July 20, 2017, which would have been Chris' 53rd birthday, his close friend Chester Bennington of Linkin Park died by suicide."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Defense of "One More Light" Sound
xref.body: Facing fan criticism for the evolving sound of Linkin Park's "One More Light" album, Chester fiercely defended the band, pushing back against critics who accused them of "selling out" or "going soft." He expressed deep personal offense, later apologizing for his harsh words. "When you make it personal, like a personal attack who we are as people, like, dude, shut up. That means I can actually have feelings about it. And for most of my time, the feelings are, I want to kill you."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Phoenix Bands
xref.body: Before moving to Los Angeles to audition for Hybrid Theory (which became Linkin Park), Chester Bennington was active in the Phoenix music scene. Around age 17 in 1993, he sang in a band with his friend Sean, initially "Sean Dattel and his friends?" and then co-formed Gray Daze, which existed from late 1993 through 1998. "We now turn our attention to the parts that came together to form Lincoln Park, specifically what Chester Bennington was up to in Phoenix before he was invited to move to LA to sing for this new group."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Warning Signs
xref.body: Despite Linkin Park's outward success, there were subtle, slow-burning, almost undetectable internal struggles within Chester Bennington that, in hindsight, pointed to a tragic end six years later. "But if anyone had taken the time to really get to know Chester Bennington, there might have been some early warning signs."

xref.title: Friendship with Chester Bennington
xref.body: Chris Cornell maintained a close friendship with Linkin Park's Chester Bennington, with both artists frequently commiserating about their shared personal demons and struggles. This bond was tragically underscored by Bennington's death by suicide a couple of months after Cornell's, on what would have been Cornell's 53rd birthday. "Chester and Chris were great, great friends, often commiserating about their various personal demons."

xref.body: Mike Shinoda reportedly designed the distinctive "big clunky set of headphones" often worn on stage by Linkin Park guitarist Brad Delson. "Mike Xionota apparently designed them."

xref.title: Influence on Linkin Park's Music
xref.body: The music for Linkin Park's song "Crawling" was directly inspired by the band members' collective love for Depeche Mode. "The music? It was inspired by collective love for Depeche Mode."

xref.title: Influence on Zero
xref.body: Alice in Chains was one of the diverse musical tastes shared among the members of the band Zero, which would later evolve into Linkin Park. "Allison Chains, the Roots, the Prodigy, you mix it all together and it all came out like this."

xref.body: The Roots were among the varied musical interests that influenced the sound of the band Zero, the precursor to Linkin Park. "Allison Chains, the Roots, the Prodigy, you mix it all together and it all came out like this."

xref.title: Influence on Zero
xref.body: The Prodigy was one of the diverse musical inspirations collectively enjoyed by the members of Zero, the band that eventually became Linkin Park. "Allison Chains, the Roots, the Prodigy, you mix it all together and it all came out like this."

xref.title: Mandatory Name Change to Linkin Park
xref.body: The band was forced to change their name from Hybrid Theory in 1999 to avoid legal issues, as another band with the same name already existed in Wales and was signed to Warner Brothers Records. This legal necessity led to the adoption of the name Linkin Park. "they really didn't have much choice because it turned out that there was already a band in Wales called Hybrid Theory, so they had to change their name to avoid any messy legal situations."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Most Successful New Metal Descendant
xref.body: Linkin Park is considered the most successful of all the bands to descend from the new metal era, having created a superior and more cohesive hybrid of alternative rock and rap. "No other band ever created a better and more cohesive hybrid of alternative rock and rap than these guys."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Musician's Expressiveness
xref.body: Chester Bennington's ability to articulate deep feelings and concepts through his music resonated with millions of fans, significantly contributing to Linkin Park's sales success. "many on the strength of Chester's abilities to express how he felt, feelings that resonated with so many others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: New Metal Era Foundation
xref.body: Linkin Park's existence and massive success (over 100 million records sold) would not have been possible had they not been "bored in the new metal era of the late 90s." "Lincoln Park would not have existed or sold 100 million records had they not been bored in the new metal era of the late 90s."

xref.title: North American Tour & Gray Days Reunion Plans
xref.body: Following the Europe tour, a short break was planned before a 29-date North American tour in support of the number one album "One More Light." Around this time, Chester was also discussing a potential reunion with Gray Days, his pre-Linkin Park band from Arizona. "Chester was talking about a reunion with Gray Days, a band from his pre-Lincoln Park days in Arizona."

xref.title: Number One Records in 2010s
xref.body: Fall Out Boy was among the artists, including Blink-182, Green Day, Coldplay, Jack White, Red Hot Chili Peppers, Slipknot, Queens of the Stone Age, Pearl Jam, Foo Fighters, U2, Linkin Park, Evanescence, and David Bowie, who achieved number one records during the 2010s. This demonstrated the continued success of rock acts in an era where hip hop was a dominant cultural force. "Link wanted a two Green Day Coldplay Jack White, Red Hotch-Lie Pepper, Slipp-Nont, Queens of the Stone Age, Pearl Jam, Foo Fighters, U2, Link and Park Follow Boy, Evan Essence, Queens of the Stone Age, and Bowie all had number one records over the course of the decade."

xref.body: In memory of Chester Bennington, Linkin Park established the "One More Light Fund," an organization dedicated to offering help and support to individuals grappling with mental health issues. "And in Chester's memory, Lincoln Park has the one more light fund, an organization that offers help to those who need it."

xref.title: Personal Life Prior to Death
xref.body: Chester had a very close relationship with his wife, Talinda, and his family, who meant everything to him. They had recently purchased a new house in a beautiful, gated community. Before the planned Linkin Park tour, he and Talinda enjoyed a two-week vacation, and he exchanged happy, positive texts with members of Stone Temple Pilots, expressing optimism for the future. "Chester and his wife and his family were super tight. They meant everything to him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Producer for Minutes to Midnight
xref.body: Rick Rubin served as the producer for Linkin Park's third studio album, Minutes to Midnight, a project that spanned approximately 18 months of work. "Lincoln Park spent about 18 months working on their third album, this time with producer Rick Rubin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Producer of Hybrid Theory
xref.body: Don Gilmore produced Linkin Park's debut album, Hybrid Theory. His demanding approach in the studio caused significant tension with the band, particularly with Chester Bennington. "He was driving them nuts with the way he was pushing them in the studio."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rejected Band Names
xref.body: Before settling on Linkin Park, the group considered other names such as "Clear" (as in transparent), "Probing Loggers," and "Platinum Lotus Foundation." "The group went through a bunch of possibilities, clear as in transparent, probing loggers. No. Platinum Lotus Foundation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Singer for Zero
xref.body: Mark Wakefield was the singer for the band Zero, the precursor to Linkin Park. He recorded the band's 1997 4-track cassette in his bedroom using a basic computer setup. "Everything was recorded in the bedroom of Singer Mark Wakefield using a root-of-entry computer setup."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Temporary Departure from Hybrid Theory
xref.body: In 1999, Farrell temporarily left Hybrid Theory to tour the Christian circuit with his former band, Tasty Snacks. This absence necessitated the hiring of two session bass players for Linkin Park's debut album, *Hybrid Theory*, with Brad Delson filling in for any unplayed parts. "Didn't help that Dave, the bass player, left a tour of the Christian circuit with Tasty Snacks that year."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Three Singers Post-Weiland – Chester Bennington Moonlighted from Linkin Park; Jeff Gutt Won Online Audition
xref.body: Scott Weiland was fired and rehired multiple times; the first replacement attempt involved David Coutts in a short-lived side project called Talk Show that failed entirely. Weiland was fired for good in 2013; he died of a drug overdose in 2016 without reconciling with the band. Chester Bennington of Linkin Park — a lifelong STP fan — was brought in for approximately two and a half years, was made an official member, toured, and recorded two tracks before returning to Linkin Park. His replacement was Jeff Gutt, found through an online audition that also briefly considered John Borja from the Philippines; Gutt had been a runner-up on Season 3 of *The X Factor* and was confirmed by fall 2017. "Chester was also a lifelong STP fan since, well, since he could remember."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: UCLA Enrollment
xref.body: Brad Delson attended UCLA, where he became roommates with Dave "Phoenix" Farrell, who would later become Linkin Park's bassist. "Brad enrolled in UCLA, where he became roommates with a bass player named Dave Phoenix Farrell."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Upcoming Tour and Reunion Plans
xref.body: At the time of his death, Chester Bennington was preparing for a 29-date Linkin Park tour and had committed to a reunion with his former band, Grey Daze, after the tour concluded. He appeared happy, secure, and in excellent physical condition. "A 29-date Lincoln Park tour was about to start, and once that was over, he'd committed to joining Gray Days, the band he was in before Lincoln Park, for a reunion."

xref.body: In addition to his role as the band's turntablist, Joseph Hahn directs Linkin Park's music videos. "Mr. Hahn, some fans, the band's turn table list. He directs videos"

xref.title: Warner Brothers' Rap Suggestion
xref.body: Warner Brothers Records suggested that Mike Shinoda of Linkin Park should learn to rap in a style similar to Fred Durst. This was part of the label's efforts to influence Linkin Park's sound. "Mike should learn to wrap like Fred Durst."

xref.title: Warner Brothers' Reggae Vocalist Suggestion
xref.body: During early discussions, Warner Brothers Records proposed bringing in a reggae vocalist named Matt Lyons to perform the rapping parts for Mike Shinoda in Linkin Park. This was one of several suggestions rejected by the band. "Or they could just bring in a reggae vocalist named Matt Lyons to do the wrapping for Mike."

xref.body: Skinny Puppy is cited as a major inspiration and influence for a long list of prominent artists including Ministry, Nine Inch Nails, Marilyn Manson, The Prodigy, Rammstein, Filter, Korn, Linkin Park, and Evanescence.
